who: Historian of Japan at Brooklyn College and CUNY; doctorate Harvard, 1947.

evidence.says: Identifies Kublin as a Brooklyn College history professor who received his doctorate at Harvard in 1947.
Identifies the specialist in modern Japanese history as professor at Brooklyn College from 1961 and associate dean of graduate studies at CUNY in 1966–1969.
The Hyman Kublin authority cites his What shall I read on Japan? (1955).
Groups What shall I read on Japan? with Japanese-history publications and a textbook contribution identifying Hyman Kublin with Brooklyn College.

notes: Name, Japanese-history works, CUNY affiliation and Harvard doctorate agree.

who: Historian of colonial Latin America and exploration, University of Arizona; PhD Berkeley, 1949.

evidence.says: Berkeley history department survey lists Ursula S. Lamb among its 1949 PhDs, records her Arizona appointment in 1974, and lists Martín Fernández de Navarrete Clears the Deck (1980).
University newspaper identifies the Arizona historian of colonial Mexico and exploration, confirms her Berkeley doctorate, and reports retirement from Arizona in 1984.
The Ursula Lamb authority is established from Martín Fernández de Navarrete clears the deck (1980), the work listed in the Berkeley profile.

notes: Institution and period fit Deeds’s 1981 doctorate; the authority work and Berkeley degree identify the same historian.

who: James Michael Laux, historian of European and French history at the University of Cincinnati.

evidence.says: Author biography in the municipal agenda packet states James Laux taught European history at Cincinnati in 1957–1989 and published books on the French Revolution and automobile history.
The September 1975 newsletter lists James Laux among University of Cincinnati history faculty taking leave.
Authority identifies James Michael Laux, also James M. Laux, from French economic policy since the liberation (1957) and The French Revolution (1982); it notes a PhD.
Alternative James B. Laux is represented by an archival collection covering 1757–1816, rather than the Cincinnati historian’s publications.

notes: The Cincinnati appointment covers Backer’s 1978 doctorate; the French-history author is James Michael Laux.

who: Matthew (Matt) Lauzon, historian of early modern Europe at Hawaii, Manoa; PhD Johns Hopkins, 2002.

evidence.says: Lauzon’s CV records Hawaii history appointments from 2002, a Johns Hopkins history PhD in 2002, Signs of Light (2010), and William Cavert as a doctoral advisee researching the French Pacific.
Authority gives Matthew Lauzon with Matt Lauzon as a variant and cites Signs of light (2010).

notes: Exact doctorate, institution, book and named doctoral advisee establish the match.

who: Ronald P. Legon, historian of ancient Greece at the University of Illinois Chicago; PhD Cornell, 1966.

evidence.says: Department lists Ronald P. Legon as history chair in 1973–1977 and 1979–1981.
May 1981 Cornell Alumni News advertises Megara by Ronald P. Legon of the University of Illinois at Chicago Circle.
Authority is established from Megara, the political history of a Greek city-state to 336 B.C. (1981), naming Ronald P. Legon.
Catalogue identifies Demos and stasis: studies in the factional politics of classical Greece by Ronald Philip Legon as a Cornell doctoral thesis of 1966.

notes: The authority’s book is explicitly attributed to the Illinois historian; field and Cornell doctorate also agree.

who: James Douglas Leighton, historian at Huron College, Western University; PhD Western Ontario, 1975.

evidence.says: Identifies J. Douglas Leighton as a professor of history at Huron College who began organizing the diocesan archives in 1976.
Cites James Douglas Leighton’s The Development of Federal Indian Policy in Canada, 1840–1890 as a Western Ontario PhD thesis, August 1975.
The James Leighton candidate is identified as a lawyer and author of Life is a game of inches, running a marketing consultancy for law firms.
Jared Leighton holds a history PhD from Nebraska–Lincoln and specializes in twentieth-century history, distinct from the Western Ontario doctorate.
John Leighton is identified as a museum director and author on nineteenth-century art, associated with the National Galleries of Scotland.

notes: Reviewed all 18 supplied authorities. They identify other given names, works and careers; none identifies James Douglas Leighton or his Western Ontario dissertation. The James Leighton candidate is explicitly a different author.

who: Sidney J. Lemelle, historian of Africa and the African diaspora at Pomona College; PhD UCLA, 1986.

evidence.says: Identifies Sidney J. Lemelle as professor of history and Africana studies, at Pomona since 1986, with a UCLA PhD.
Lists Sidney Lemelle’s 1986 dissertation, Capital, State, and Labor: A History of the Gold Mining Industry in Colonial Tanganyika, 1890–1942.
Herbert G. Ruffin II’s CV names Sid Lemelle of Pomona among advisors of his 2007 Claremont Graduate University doctorate and gives the matching Uninvited Neighbors dissertation title.
Authority identifies Sidney J. Lemelle from Capital, state, and labor (1986), matching the UCLA dissertation.

notes: Exact doctoral work and year match the authority; the student’s CV directly confirms supervision.

who: Connie L. Lester, historian of the U.S. South and agriculture at Mississippi State and UCF; PhD Tennessee, 1998.

evidence.says: Connie L. Lester’s CV records a Tennessee, Knoxville history PhD in 1998, Mississippi State employment in 1999–2005, and Up From the Mudsills of Hell: The Farmers’ Alliance, Populism, and Progressive Agriculture in Tennessee, 1870–1915 (2006).
University dissertation record names Connie Lester as advisor for Stephanie Renee Rolph’s Displacing race, awarded a history PhD in May 2009.
Authority identifies Connie L. Lester from The Farmers’ Alliance, populism, and progressive agriculture in Tennessee, 1870–1915 (2006), matching her CV.
Alternative authority identifies C. Edwards Lester as Charles Edwards Lester, an author, clergyman and journalist, with works including Our first hundred years (1875).

notes: Exact degree, publication and student supervision establish Connie L. Lester; Charles Edwards Lester is a different author.
